root_cause.text: bpf_prog_test_run_skb() in net/bpf/test_run.c trusted skb->protocol after eth_type_trans() and accessed ip_hdr(skb)/ipv6_hdr(skb) to populate socket fields without first validating that the skb head actually contained a full IPv4 or IPv6 header.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly says it "may access ip_hdr(skb) or ipv6_hdr(skb) even when the provided test input only contains an Ethernet header," and the patch adds early `skb_headlen(skb) < sizeof(struct iphdr)` / `sizeof(struct ipv6hdr)` checks that return `-EINVAL` before any `ip_hdr(skb)` or `ipv6_hdr(skb)` dereference.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly says it "may access ip_hdr(skb) or ipv6_hdr(skb) even when the provided test input only contains an Ethernet header," and the patch adds early `skb_headlen(skb) < sizeof(struct iphdr)` / `sizeof(struct ipv6hdr)` checks that return `-EINVAL` before any `ip_hdr(skb)` or `ipv6_hdr(skb)` dereference.

intent_record.intent_summary: Validate that skb data contains a full IPv4/IPv6 header before populating socket fields, returning -EINVAL for truncated packets.
intent_record.what: In bpf_prog_test_run_skb(), the IPv4 and IPv6 protocol cases were changed to first check whether skb_headlen(skb) is smaller than sizeof(struct iphdr) or sizeof(struct ipv6hdr), and if so set ret = -EINVAL and jump to out; the assignments to sk->sk_family and the source/destination address fields were moved after these checks and are now unconditional once the header-length check passes.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now rejects test packets whose linear skb head is too short to contain a full IPv4 or IPv6 header, instead of proceeding with partially initialized socket fields or reading header data conditionally while still setting the socket family. This prevents invalid packet inputs from being treated as usable and avoids accessing protocol header fields when the header is not fully present.

grouping_result.intent: Validate that skb data contains a full IPv4/IPv6 header before populating socket fields, returning -EINVAL for truncated packets.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by adding IPv4/IPv6 header length validation before accessing ip_hdr(skb)/ipv6_hdr(skb) after trusting skb->protocol, and rejects truncated packets with -EINVAL.

candidates.rationale: The root cause is trusting skb->protocol after eth_type_trans() to decide header type without first ensuring the skb head contains a full corresponding IP header. This switch is the control point that performs that trust.
This populates socket state based solely on skb->protocol before validating that a full IPv4 header is present, embodying the improper trust described in the root cause.

This directly dereferences the IPv4 header derived from skb data and reads fields to populate the socket, which is unsafe when skb->protocol is trusted without prior validation of a complete IPv4 header.
This assigns IPv6 socket family based only on skb->protocol before confirming the skb head actually contains a full IPv6 header, matching the root cause.
This directly accesses the IPv6 header to populate socket fields, which is vulnerable if skb->protocol is trusted but the skb head does not contain a full IPv6 header.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement directly dereferences the IPv4 header from skb data and reads a field without first validating that the skb head contains a complete IPv4 header, which is the core unsafe access described in the root cause.
This statement directly dereferences the IPv6 header from skb data and reads a field without first validating that the skb head contains a complete IPv6 header, matching the root cause.

This is the control point that trusts skb->protocol after eth_type_trans() to choose IPv4 vs IPv6 handling, without first validating that the skb head actually contains the corresponding full IP header.

In the shown snippet, there is no code accessing `ip_hdr(skb)`, `ipv6_hdr(skb)`, or populating socket fields from those headers, so the vulnerable construct described in the root cause is absent from this function body excerpt. Therefore, for the stated vulnerability, this function does not contain the vulnerable construct, and it also does not show the corresponding fix.
